newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity jumps to new highs on gas, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity jumps to new highs on gas, cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity jumped to new contract highs Tuesday, spurred by strength in the western spot cash power market and a spike in natural gas futures, market sources said.
"It was an all-day rally," said an East Coast electricity broker.
The power complex showed signs of easing early afternoon, but roared back with the sharp rise in Henry Hub natgas futures, brokers and traders said.
"It was coming off but then natural gas rallied up," said a Houston futures trader.
The NYMEX June Henry Hub gas contracts ended up 8.9 cents at $2.309 per million British thermal units. In the western gas market, June San Juan deliveries rose to $2.00-2.05 from $1.87-1.91 Monday.
Market sources said sharp gains in recent sessions have forced players, especially utilities to cover their positions.
Compared with a week ago, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures gained $3.03 a megawatt hour (MWh) or 22.8 percent and June Palo Verde (PV) $3.65 or 19.4 percent.
June COB settled up 88 cents at $16.33 after posting a new life-of-contract high at $16.50. July COB ended up 99 cents at $17.89. Other active COB months finished up 20 cents to $1.
June PV settled up $1.12 at $22.50 after settling a new contract high at $22.60. July PV ended up 90 cents at $25.75, the day's session high. Deferred PV contracts finished 20 to 94 cents higher.
Day-ahead peak prices at COB were steady at $16.50-17.00, while those at PV climbed to $1.50-2.00 to $23.50-24.00.

Generation capacity in the western U.S. remained limited, with about 8,000 megawatts in the West said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
Restart of the 550 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power complex in Wyoming was planned to restart tomorrow, industry sources said.
Although there is growing concern that the complex may be over-valued, power futures are expected to continue their current uptrend Wednesday, market sources said.
"It's safe to assume, they'll try to push it higher," the Houston trader said.
NYMEX estimated 754 COB and 851 PV contracts were sold, sharply higher than yesterday's 476 COB and 347 PV lots.
